plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges towards bidding your true value minus a small amount. This is because bidding too high risks overpaying, while bidding too low risks losing the item even when it's worth more than the bid. Since this is round 1 and there is no previous history, I will bid slightly below my value to attempt to win at a reasonable price. I will bid $24.5.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the minimum increment. Since values are between $0 and $49, and the second-highest bid determines the price, a bid of $0.1 ensures winning if my value is higher than others' and minimizes losses if others have much higher values. My value is $3, so a small bid is reasonable.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bid your value multiplied by 2/3. This is because any higher bid risks overpaying, and any lower bid risks letting someone else win an item you value highly. Since this is round 1 and there is no history, I will follow this strategy. My value is $26, so 2/3 * $26 = $17.33. I will round this to the nearest tenth.
